subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After an opt-in maintenance timeout releases a foreground turn, should OpenClaw continue coalescing same-session maintenance until the original plugin worker settles, or should it establish a new cancellable maintenance contract before allowing replacement workers?
rationale: The command queue can release scheduling ownership without terminating the plugin-owned work, and neither the existing ContextEngine maintenance seam nor this PR proves a safe concurrent-maintenance contract.

options.title: Retain physical-worker coalescing
options.body: Keep a separate per-session settlement record after timeout, fence the timed-out worker, and schedule at most one rerun only after that original worker settles.

options.title: Design explicit cancellation
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved ContextEngine cancellation/abort contract, then permit replacement maintenance only after the old worker acknowledges cancellation.

recommendation.title: Retain physical-worker coalescing
recommendation.body: Keep a separate per-session settlement record after timeout, fence the timed-out worker, and schedule at most one rerun only after that original worker settles.

likelyOwner.reason: The current proposal author is the only concrete technical routing candidate established by the supplied branch history; permanent API direction still needs an OpenClaw maintainer decision.
